title: Dry-Erase Blueprint — Startup Whiteboard Explainer
description: A whiteboard-native template that captures the raw energy of an in-room brainstorm: black dry-erase strokes, architecture boxes and arrows with a handwriting waver, and a single red marker circle that does the arguing. The faint smudge in the corner signals that thinking happened here.
philosophy: This design exists for the moment when a technical founder explains a system to five people crowded around a real board — not a Figma file. It refuses digital polish, drop shadows, and brand consistency in favor of legible, earned mess that signals active cognition. The red callout circle is the slide's entire thesis; the rest of the diagram is supporting evidence. It is built for rooms, not stages, and for architects and engineers who would rather draw than design.
goodFor: Technical architecture walkthroughs with 3–6 labeled nodes and directional arrows
Internal team brainstorm recaps exported to PDF or shared async
Engineering onboarding flows where box-and-arrow clarity beats visual flair
Early-stage founder explainer slides for seed-round technical due diligence
avoidFor: Investor pitch decks requiring polished brand consistency and typography control
Data-heavy quarterly reviews with charts, tables, or dense numerical grids
Large-screen conference keynotes where subtle smudge textures read as printing errors
Consumer-facing marketing where the hand-drawn looseness undercuts credibility
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide evokes the opening frame of a live whiteboard session: raw strokes, slightly wavering letterforms, and one emphatic red-marker circle that declares the deck's subject before a word is processed. Composition breathes with purposeful emptiness — most of the field stays unoccupied white so the circled title and a stray diagrammatic fragment feel genuinely authored, not placed. The overall mood is earned mess over designed polish: cognitive, mid-thought, belonging to a room of engineers leaning forward. Avoid gradients, centered symmetry, drop shadows, and anything implying a design tool was opened.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; title text anchored in columns 2–10 with a deliberately ragged right edge, leaving negative space that reads as unfinished-by-design. A hand-drawn enclosing box or wobbly underline sits directly beneath the main title, drawn slightly off-axis. Subtitle or deck descriptor drops two line-heights below with reduced visual weight, separated by void rather than a rule. A single loose architecture arrow-and-node fragment occupies the lower-right corner as a silent supporting motif — no page number, no header band.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a snapshot of a real board mid-explanation — not cleaned up, not composed, just captured. The overall rhythm is asymmetric and diagram-driven: labeled architecture boxes connected by wavering directional arrows form the visual core, while a single red marker circle isolates and argues for one node above all others. Surrounding whitespace is not designed breathing room but the natural residue of a marker that ran out of real estate. Avoid any hint of digital gloss, icon libraries, or geometric perfection; even the straightest line should carry a slight human tremor.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed whiteboard surface with a loose 12-column grid; the architecture diagram occupies roughly columns 1–10, leaving the right edge as unintentional negative space. Slide label sits upper-left in a small hand-lettered cap treatment — no header band. Three to six labeled rectangular nodes are arranged in a two-row staggered layout connected by directional arrows of uneven weight; the thesis node is enclosed by the red callout circle placed at visual center-right. A faint smudge texture bleeds into the bottom-left corner. Page reference sits bottom-right at minimum size with no surrounding decoration.
